topic: Trunk or hatch won't stay up: worn gas struts, not the latch
mode: PRODUCTION (pack only, no live reel-canary call)
negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: Your trunk or hatch slowly sinks back down after you open it, or you're propping it up yourself.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro shot, open trunk lid seen from the side, gas strut rod visible along the hinge, lid held near full-open angle, slow push-in, no hands or driver visible, shallow depth of field
stockSearchTerms: car trunk open side view strut

beats.narration: That's not the latch. It's the gas struts, the two rods that hold the lid open, losing pressure.
beats.visualPrompt: Close macro shot of a single gas strut cylinder removed and resting on a workbench, chrome rod and black cylinder body visible, static locked shot with subtle rack-focus shift, no hands

beats.narration: Each strut is a sealed gas cylinder. Years of heat and cold cycling wear the internal seal, so pressure leaks out and it can't hold the lid's weight anymore.
beats.visualPrompt: Slow macro orbit around the strut's seal end, subtle oily residue visible near the cylinder base, soft workshop lighting, slow orbital camera move, no hands or text

beats.narration: Quick check: push up on the lid. If it holds steady, the latch is fine. If it drifts back down, it's the struts.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro shot of the open trunk lid drifting slowly downward under its own weight, subtle motion blur on the lid edge, no hands, no on-screen text

beats.narration: Don't let it drop on you while you're loading groceries. We can swap the struts before one lets go completely.
beats.visualPrompt: Same framing and lens as beat 1 (open trunk lid, side view, strut visible), lid now held fully and steadily open, warm shop-bay light in the background, static locked shot, no faces or logos
stockSearchTerms: auto repair shop bay warm light
